query: The Helmet in the Boathouse The old diving helmet is where you left it, on the workbench by the doors. Somebody has oiled the rope since last time. The lake is still, and under it the bell is waiting. Dive again You go down slower this time, and further. The bell lies on its side, and around its rim, letters: a name you don't know. You surface gasping, and you keep the name. The cold finds you again, halfway down. You come up blue and shaking, with nothing but the certainty that it's down there. Not today You put the helmet back on the bench. The bell can wait one more day. It has waited sixty years.
